full_judgment:
Mr. Gour Gopal Saha, J: This rule is directed against the order dated 17.6.1984 passed by the learned Munsif, Nazirpur in the District of Pirojpur, in Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1984 under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure restoring Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1984 under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted a suit for partition on declaration of title in the suit land in the 2nd Court of Munsif at Pirojpur in which opposite party No.1 was defendant No. 13. Defendant opposite party No.2 contested the suit by filing written• statement while defendant Nos. 2, 15 and 20, though filed written statements, did not eventually contest the suit and some other defendants prayed for separate saliams. The suit was ultimately decreed on 30.1.1982. Thereafter opposite party No. 1 filed Title Appeal No. 39 of 1982 before the District Judge, Bakerganj against the aforesaid judgment and, decree but eventually the said appeal was dis-missed on 9.6.1983.
3. Opposite party No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 51 of 1982 before the 2nd Court of Munsif at Pirojpur for setting aside the decree passed on 30.1.82 under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the said Miscellaneous Case was subsequently re-numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1984. The said Miscellaneous Case was eventually fixed for peremptory hearing on 29.5.1984 but as the petitioner was absent on that dale and took no step in the matter the case was dismissed for default. Thereafter opposite party No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1984 in the said Court under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1984 alleging inter alia that he was attacked with diarrhea is a result of which he could not appear before the Court on the fateful day on 29.5.1984 which lead to the dismissed of the case for default. In due course of time 15.7.1984 was fixed for peremptory hearing of Misc. Case No. 71 of 1984 but on the application of opposite party No. 1 the date of a hearing was shifted back to 17.6.1984 and on that date the learned Munsif allowed the said Miscellaneous case and set aside the order dated 29.5.1984 by which Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1984 was dis-missed and restored the case to its file and number. It is against this order allowing Miscellaneous Case No.71 of 1984 that the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the present rule.

 4. No one appears to support the rule. 

5. No one also appears to oppose the rule. 

6. I have perused the impugned order dated 17.6.84 by which the learned Munsif allowed Miscellaneous Case No. 71 Of 1984 under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure without assigning any reason whatsoever. It also appears from the impugned order that although the case was fixed for hearing on 17.6.1984, it was shifted back to 17.6.1984 on the prayer of opposite party No. 1 and on that very dale Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1984 under Order 9 rule 4 of the Civil Procedure was allowed in the name of interest of justice. 

7. An application under order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure may be allowed only when the petitioner satisfies the Court that there was sufficient cause for non-appearance of the petitioner when the case was called on for hearing. From the impugned order it is evident that the learned Munsif completely ignored the clear mandate of Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure in passing the impugned order, leaving the field of fact and straying to fiction. 

8. It is well-settled that the inherent power of the Court under section 151 C.P.C. can be resorted to in the interest of justice only when there is no specific provision In the Code of Civil Procedure to meet a particular situation and that too for preventing an abuse of the process of the Court or an apparent injustice. But in our case under review, the petitioner sought relief under the provision or Order 9 rule 4 C.P.C., where relief could be given to him if he was able to successfully meet the requirements of law in joined by the said Order. In the face of specific provisions of law under Order 9 rule 4 C.P.C. requiring necessary proof for the satisfaction of the Court to set aside the dis-missal of suit/case for default of the plaintiff or the petitioner, an applicant can succeed in his case only on the merit of his own case and not an any other extraneous considerations. When there is a specific provision of law for giving relief to an aggrieved party but the requirements of law are not met, the Court has no power to dole out gratuitions relief in the name of "interest of justice" or "ends of justice". The Court must not use these expressions lightly and capriciously as it would tend to defeat justice but use the same according to sound judicial principles for ensuring real justice. We may derive instant support of this view in the case of Mst. Khairunnesa Vs. Zabaida Nahar @ Jharns and others reported in 17 B.L.D. (AD), 51. 

9. In this case admittedly the petitioner of Misc. Case No. 71 of 1984 did not examine any witness in support of his case. Except his uncorroborated statements incorporated in his application under Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure there is absolutely nothing on record to prove that he was pre-vented by any sufficient cause from appearing before the Court when the case was called a for hearing and this lead to the dis-missal of his case for default. In the absence of any evidence before him providing necessary satisfaction that the petitioner was really prevented by sufficient cause from appearing before the Court on the fateful day, the learned trial Court clearly erred in law in allowing Miscellaneous Case no. 71 of 1984 completely ignoring the mandatory provisions of Order 9 rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The impugned order thus evidently suffers from legal infirmity which can-not be sustained. 

10. In the result, the rule succeeds and it is made absolute without any order as to costs.

11. The impugned order dated 17.6.84 passed by the learned Munsif. Nazirpur is set aside and Miscellaneous Case No.7I of 1984 is sent back on remand to the trial Court for decision according to law. The learned Musif" (now Assistant Judge), Nazirpur is directed to dispose of Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1984 within a period of 3 (three) months positively from the dale of the receipt of this order, after giving opportunities to the parties to represent their respective cases but without granting adjournments except on compelling reasons. 

12. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated. 

13. Communicate this order to the learned Munsil (new Assistant Judge) Nazirpur at once. 

End.
